records.text: - Continuous Ambulatory ECG (14-day Zio XT monitor):  Image Title: Rhythm Strip From Zio Monitor  Image Description: The rhythm strip shows dual sinus node activity with:  - Donor sinus node rate estimated at 62 beats per minute  - Native sinus node rate estimated at 70 beats per minute  - A pause in ventricular activation interrupted by a junctional escape beat after 4.5 seconds  - Smaller P waves visible within the pause, dissociated from the active rhythm  - Prior 12-lead ECGs: Showed intermittent deflections with diminutive native P waves.

Need the post-transplant echocardiogram report, current immunosuppressant levels with renal function, and documented orthostatic vital signs plus medication administration times during symptomatic episodes, as these are essential to confirm sinus node dysfunction with bradyarrhythmia as the cause of episodic hypotension and to exclude graft rejection or metabolic contributors.

Need the Zio monitor symptom-event diary with patient-activated events and corresponding rhythm strips, to determine whether dizziness/near-syncope coincided with the 4.5-second pause and junctional escape; this correlation is critical to confirm symptomatic bradyarrhythmia and support sinus node dysfunction as the mechanism.

Need the patient's ambulatory blood pressure monitoring report and medication administration timing records to confirm episodic hypotension and its correlation with the 4.5-second pause, along with a 12-lead ECG and transplant operative details (biatrial vs bicaval) to assess sinus node dysfunction risk.

bindings.label: Patient presented with new-onset dizziness while sitting and episodes of near-syncope without loss of consciousness

Patient is a man in his 70s with history of orthotopic heart transplant performed using biatrial surgical technique; posttransplant history includes grade 1 cardiac allograft vasculopathy, toxic multinodular goiter status postthyroidectomy, and associated tremors treated with propranolol.
Two weeks prior, his cardiologist measured low blood pressure and stopped amlodipine treatment, after which symptoms improved.
Physical examination at presentation: patient was normotensive and cardiac examination was unremarkable.
Medication-induced hypotension
Cardiac graft/arrhythmic cause
Autonomic/orthostatic cause
Orthostatic blood pressure measurements were not obtained during the evaluation
Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring was not performed to evaluate episodic hypotension
Timing of medication administration relative to dizziness episodes was not documented
Episodic hypotension is the likely mechanism underlying the patient's dizziness and near-syncope
Retrieved Zio monitor reveals dual sinus node activity with a 4.5-second ventricular pause and junctional escape
Symptomatic bradyarrhythmia due to sinus node dysfunction or transplant-related autonomic denervation is contributing to the patient's dizziness and near-syncope
Episodic hypotension secondary to bradyarrhythmia from sinus node dysfunction after biatrial heart transplant
Episodic orthostatic hypotension due to transplant-related autonomic denervation
Episodic hypotension due to ongoing propranolol therapy
Episodic hypotension due to cardiac allograft vasculopathy-related ischemia
Symptom-event diary correlation was not documented, leaving the temporal relationship between the 4.5-second ventricular pause and dizziness/near-syncope unconfirmed
